subject: history_social
passage: In the first century CE, Roman engineers built an aqueduct to carry water about 50 kilometers to the city of Nîmes, in what is now southern France. The aqueduct had no pumps. Instead, its channel sloped downward very gently, dropping only about 12 meters over the whole route, so that gravity alone kept the water moving. To cross a deep river valley, the channel ran along the top of a tall stone bridge, the Pont du Gard.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the kinds of stone used to build the Pont du Gard
choices.B: To argue that Roman aqueducts were better built than modern water systems
choices.C: To describe daily life in the city of Nîmes in the first century CE
choices.D: To explain how a Roman aqueduct carried water a long distance without pumps

explanation.why: The text says the aqueduct "had no pumps" and then explains what it used instead: a channel that sloped gently so that "gravity alone kept the water moving," plus a bridge to cross a valley. Its purpose is to explain how the aqueduct worked.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The Pont du Gard is called a "tall stone bridge," but the text does not describe the stone; the bridge is one detail of the route.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares the aqueduct with modern water systems.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nîmes is named only as the aqueduct's destination; the text says nothing about life there.
explanation.D: Correct. The text explains that a gentle downward slope let gravity move water about 50 kilometers without any pumps.
